## 6. Cross-cutting suites

### 6.1 Smoke suite

Eleven checks, under two minutes, run in **every** environment including after an install at a school
— which is the point, since the failures this catches are environment-specific and would not appear in
CI. Any failure stops the pipeline or blocks the install.

| ID | Req | Check | Fails if |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-SMOKE-01 | NFR-STORE-03 | A clean virtualenv install completes with no npm toolchain, no build step, no server process | Any additional install step is required |
| TC-SMOKE-02 | FR-CONF-01 | `resolve_run_config` succeeds for the configured profile and reports it | Profile unresolvable or defaulted |
| TC-SMOKE-03 | FR-STORE-01, FR-STORE-02 | All four tiers open, migrate to current, and report `journal_mode = wal` | Any tier fails to open or migrate |
| TC-SMOKE-04 | FR-STORE-09 | The data directory exists with owner-only permissions and is not inside a temp path | Wrong mode, or an insecure location |
| TC-SMOKE-05 | FR-PROV-01, FR-PROV-02 | The bound provider answers one trivial completion and reports capabilities | Provider unreachable, or capabilities undeclared |
| TC-SMOKE-06 | FR-PROV-14 | On `cloud-hosted`, zero-retention routing is confirmed for every panel model | Any model unconfirmed |
| TC-SMOKE-07 | FR-CONSOLE-05 | The console binds to loopback and serves its index; it refuses to start on `cloud-hosted` | Bound beyond loopback, or started on the cloud profile |
| TC-SMOKE-08 | FR-INGEST-02 | One two-page fixture PDF ingests end to end and produces a `document` row | Ingestion fails, or `transcriber_ref` is null |
| TC-SMOKE-09 | FR-ORCH-01 | A three-unit run enumerates, executes and completes against the fixture provider | Enumeration or completion fails |
| TC-SMOKE-10 | FR-GRADE-01 | That run produces a `submission_grade` for every submission | Any submission ungraded |
| TC-SMOKE-11 | FR-CONF-09 | The build version, resolved model builds and backend profile are all reported and match configuration | Version drift between what is deployed and what is reported |

### 6.2 System / E2E journeys

Three journeys, taken from design §4.2. Deliberately three and not ten: E2E flakiness scales with
count, and everything permutable is covered at lower rungs. Each has a failure-path variant. All run
against `F-SYNTH` with the recorded-fixture provider in CI, and once per release against a live
backend on E3.

#### TC-E2E-01 — Package setup, from four PDFs to a published locked version

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Requirements | FR-INGEST-32, FR-SETUP-02, FR-SETUP-16, FR-PKG-01, FR-CONSOLE-06 |
| Design ref | §4.2.1 |
| Level | Rung 4 |
| Priority | P0 |

**Happy path**: a teacher uploads assessment, reference, rubric and marked calibration papers; the
inventory is proposed and confirmed (blocking); answer keys are supplied (blocking); the rubric is
read back into criteria and even band sets; decomposability is classified; dependencies are proposed
and declined; the grade policy is skipped and the default recorded; the prefix budget is checked; the
version publishes and the §6.2 lock takes effect. **Oracle**: the published package matches its golden
manifest, and a post-publication edit to any locked field raises `SchemaLockViolation`.

**Failure variant**: the rubric PDF fails V0. It surfaces on the **teacher upload screen**, not in the
operator quarantine queue (`FR-INGEST-32`), and setup remains resumable from that point.

#### TC-E2E-02 — The overnight run, with zero teacher action

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Requirements | NFR-SYS-04, FR-GRADE-01, FR-GRADE-10, FR-ORCH-02, FR-JUDGE-02 |
| Design ref | §4.2.2 |
| Level | Rung 4 |
| Priority | P0 — this is the standing gate of §4.8 item 5 |

**Happy path**: 350 submissions ingest (9 quarantine); the run starts with the backend fixed; units
enumerate and a cost estimate is shown; Sweep 1 runs in topological order; the integrity gate runs;
deterministic criteria are scored by lookup; Sweep 2 runs judge-first; verdicts aggregate to median
bands with points mapped once; escalations enqueue in-transaction; synthesis runs L1 then L2; the run
completes and **every** grade finalizes with no teacher action at any point. **Oracle**: 341 grades
exist, coverage is recorded per grade, provisional grades are labelled, and the whole journey is
compared against a committed baseline result set.

**Failure variants**, each run as a separate execution: (a) `SIGKILL` at a random point, then
`resume()` — the result set must equal the uninterrupted baseline (`RES-04..07`); (b) the provider goes
unavailable mid-run — the run pauses on the same backend and resumes; (c) a criterion trips the
escalation breaker — it is marked `ungradeable_by_panel`, scored single-judge provisional, and
surfaces in the rollup, and the run still completes.

#### TC-E2E-03 — The review morning, and the honest residual

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Requirements | FR-REVIEW-02, FR-REVIEW-11, FR-STATS-01, FR-GRADE-09, FR-CONSOLE-13 |
| Design ref | §4.2.3 |
| Level | Rung 4 |
| Priority | P0 |

**Happy path**: the teacher states 30 minutes; 10 are reserved for the blind sample **before** ranking;
40 of 790 flagged items are shown and 750 stay provisional, stated in the header; a group action
covers 210 identical items; the blind sample runs with system output unreachable; κ is computed from
blind judged labels only with n attached; the whole-grade sample draws from the auto-accepted
population; the class finalizes in one action naming its coverage. **Oracle**: label rows match the
actions taken with the right `saw_system_output` values; the agreement figure's n equals the blind
label count and not the total label count.

**Failure variant**: the teacher does none of it. Grades finalize anyway at window lapse, the
validation record does **not** advance, and the console reports "no new validation evidence for this
administration" rather than reusing a prior figure (`FR-REVIEW-13`, `FR-STATS-11`, `FR-CONSOLE-24`).

### 6.3 User acceptance tests

Written in the teacher's and operator's language against the design's business goals. Each names who
runs it, with what data, and what constitutes sign-off. `NFR-SYS-07`'s time budgets are acceptance
criteria here, not aspirations — and the design is explicit that teacher time must not scale with
class size at any point.

| UAT ID | Req | Business goal | Role | Scenario (Given / When / Then) | Data | Sign-off criterion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UAT-01 | NFR-SYS-04, FR-GRADE-01 | Grades arrive without me doing anything overnight | Teacher | **Given** a set-up package and 350 scanned submissions, **when** the operator starts a run in the evening and nobody touches the system, **then** in the morning every submission that passed ingestion has a complete, exportable grade with feedback | 350 real-medium scans | The teacher confirms a full set of grades exists and can be exported to the school's format, with no action having been taken |
| UAT-02 | NFR-SETUP-01, NFR-SYS-07 | Setting up an assessment takes minutes, not an evening | Teacher | **Given** four PDFs, **when** the teacher runs setup, **then** they answer two blocking screens and at most six optional confirmations | A 15-criterion rubric | Total elapsed teacher time is under 20 minutes, timed; the teacher can state what the system will do with the rubric |
| UAT-03 | NFR-CALIB-01 | Calibration is a short conversation, not a project | Teacher | **Given** a rubric with ambiguities, **when** calibration runs, **then** at most six questions are asked, each answerable from two student examples side by side | A rubric with known ambiguity | Under 15 minutes; the teacher agrees each question was about their rubric rather than about the model |
| UAT-04 | FR-REVIEW-01, FR-REVIEW-04 | My 30 minutes are spent on the items that matter | Teacher | **Given** 790 flagged items and a 30-minute budget, **when** the queue is built, **then** the teacher works top-down and the header tells them honestly what they did not see | A completed run | The teacher rates the shown items as worth reviewing, and reports the residual message as informative rather than alarming (HLD §11.9 question 4) |
| UAT-05 | FR-REVIEW-10, FR-CONSOLE-07 | Editing a band rather than a number is workable | Teacher | **Given** a score the teacher disagrees with, **when** they change it, **then** they select a band with its descriptor and never type a number | A run with disagreements | The teacher can complete every correction they wanted to make; they report band-only editing as a relief or a constraint, recorded either way (HLD §11.9 question 3) |
| UAT-06 | FR-INGEST-30, FR-CONSOLE-11 | Scanning problems are mine, marking decisions are the teacher's | Operator | **Given** 9 quarantined submissions, **when** the operator opens quarantine, **then** they see only ingestion problems with the page image, and can resolve or close each as unresolvable | A cohort with real scan failures | The operator resolves every item without needing a marking judgement; no quarantine item ever appears in the teacher's queue |
| UAT-07 | FR-GRADE-06, FR-GRADE-04 | A provisional grade is still a usable grade | Teacher | **Given** grades with provisional inputs, **when** the teacher exports, **then** each grade is complete, marked provisional, and states its coverage | A run with an exhausted review budget | The teacher is willing to issue the provisional grades, or states specifically why not |
| UAT-08 | FR-CONSOLE-24, FR-STATS-11 | The system tells me when it does not know | Teacher | **Given** a package never administered to this population, **when** the teacher opens it, **then** they see "no validation data for this population" rather than a number | An imported package | The teacher correctly describes what the system does and does not know about this package |

### 6.4 Performance scenarios

One scenario per quantified NFR. Unquantified performance claims are in §2.3, not here. Every result
names its environment: a number from E1 or E3 is **not** evidence about E4.

| Perf ID | NFR | Load profile | Duration | Dataset | Metric | Threshold | Env |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PERF-01 | NFR-ORCH-01, R10 | A full uniform-depth run, continuous batching at the profile concurrency ceiling | To completion | `F-SYNTH` 350 × 15 criteria (~23,000 units) | Wall clock | Fits the overnight window with margin; ~1.7 h at uniform depth is the **hypothesis**, recorded not asserted | E4 |
| PERF-02 | NFR-INGEST-01 | Fully parallel ingestion at the concurrency ceiling | To completion | 350 submissions × ~4 pages (~1,400 VLM calls) | Wall clock | Same order of magnitude as the scoring pass; **measured, not estimated** | E4 |
| PERF-03 | NFR-ORCH-01 | Enumeration and scheduling only, provider stubbed | 23,000 units | `F-SYNTH` | Scheduling overhead per unit | < 5 ms | E1 |
| PERF-04 | NFR-JUDGE-01, NFR-PROV-02 | 32 concurrent scoring calls in one (judge, question, criterion) batch | 10 min | 350 submissions | `cache_hit_rate`, `cached_prefix_tokens` | High and stable; a drop below the run's historical band is a **build failure**, per HLD §9.7, not a note. **Same measurement as `TC-PROV-22`** (§5.2), which is its `M-PROV`-side entry; this row owns the profile, threshold and environment | E3 |
| PERF-05 | NFR-STORE-01 | Sustained write load | 60 s | Synthetic write units | Write units per second | ≥ 200/s with no queue growth | E1 |
| PERF-06 | NFR-INTEG-01, NFR-AGG-03, NFR-DET-01 | The zero-model stages, measured against a run with them disabled | Full run | `F-SYNTH` | Added wall clock | Integrity < 1% of run wall clock; aggregation microseconds each; all deterministic criteria for 350 students < 5 s | E1 |
| PERF-07 | NFR-GRADE-03 | Grading and rollup | Single pass | 350 submissions | Wall clock, model calls | < 30 s, zero model calls | E1 |
| PERF-08 | NFR-REVIEW-01, NFR-CONSOLE-01 | Queue build and render; rollup render | Single request | 350-student run, ~800 flagged | Render time | Queue < 2 s, rollup < 3 s | E1 |
| PERF-09 | NFR-ORCH-06, NFR-STORE-06 | Volume: 40,000 ledger units; full run footprint | To completion | Extended `F-SYNTH` | Lease/complete/progress latency; disk footprint | No degradation at 40,000 vs 23,000; footprint < 500 MB | E1 |
| PERF-10 | NFR-SYS-05 | **The release gate.** Full-pipeline acceptance run: 350 representative submissions in the real medium, a mixed-format paper, the real OCR stage, target models at target quantization, the real serving stack at target concurrency, real storage, and one deliberate mid-run kill | Overnight | Real consented corpus | The HLD §8.5 gate table in full: wall clock within the window with margin; peak memory under the profile ceiling; aggregate throughput within range of projection; high prefix cache hit rate; model swap time in minutes not per criterion; no sustained thermal throttling; OCR triage time within the teacher-minute budget; units fail but the run completes; resume correct after kill; disk growth within free space | All ten sub-criteria met | **E4 only** — the design states that a green CI pipeline is no evidence for this gate, and this plan repeats it |

### 6.5 Security tests

The threat model is a local, offline, single-user system with one internet-facing option
(`cloud-hosted`) and one genuinely untrusted input surface (submitted PDFs). Adapted from STRIDE and
OWASP rather than transplanted: there are no accounts, so authentication and authorization probes are
replaced by boundary-refusal probes, and that substitution is the finding, not an omission.

| Sec ID | Req | Trust boundary | Threat (STRIDE / OWASP) | Probe | Expected defense |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-01 | FR-CONF-11, NFR-CONF-02 | Process to disk and logs | Information disclosure / A02 | Run with sentinel credentials at DEBUG; scrape every persisted row, log record and exception | No credential value anywhere; credentials read only from environment or OS secret store |
| SEC-02 | FR-CONF-08 | Machine to remote provider | Information disclosure / A01 | Attempt a `cloud-hosted` run against a cohort with `consent_class = 'real'` and against one with none declared | `ConsentGateError` in both; the override path is explicit and audited |
| SEC-03 | FR-PROV-14, NFR-SYS-03 | Machine to remote provider | Information disclosure | Start a `cloud-hosted` run where one panel model cannot confirm zero-retention, over the injected `retention_answers` source (`FR-PROV-15`); and again where the answer is absent, empty or hedged | `RetentionPolicyError`; the run does not start, and **no payload is dispatched before the check completes** (`CT-PROV-13`, observed through `on_dispatch`). The fail-closed half is asserted here because this probe's oracle needs it: "unconfirmed" must cover an ambiguous answer or an exception-type assertion passes against a gate that reads `"unknown"` as yes. `TC-PROV-17` (`TS-05`) is the same rule against the live API's real response shapes |
| SEC-04 | NFR-PROV-04, NFR-JUDGE-04 | Prompt payloads | Information disclosure | Scan every assembled payload in a full run against the roster's real names | `student_ref` only; no name in any payload |
| SEC-05 | FR-INGEST-33 | PDF parser | Elevation of privilege | Ingest each `F-ADV-PDF` active-content fixture | Stripped or quarantined; **zero** VLM calls for anything unsanitizable |
| SEC-06 | FR-INGEST-34 | PDF parser | Denial of service | Ingest the decompression bomb, the 100k-page file, the 60000×60000-pixel image | Quarantined before allocation; peak memory bounded; wall-clock ceiling enforced |
| SEC-07 | NFR-INGEST-08 | PDF parser | Fail-open | Inject an exception inside the stripper and inside each resource-bound evaluation | Every error resolves to quarantine, never to processing |
| SEC-08 | FR-INGEST-21 | PDF parser | Denial of service / malformed input | Ingest an encrypted PDF, a zero-page PDF, a truncated PDF, and a PDF with a cyclic object graph | Each quarantines as `unreadable` with no hang and no unhandled exception |
| SEC-09 | FR-STORE-06, FR-STORE-09 | Filesystem | Path traversal / A01 | Call `get()` and `path()` directly with a non-hex `content_hash` (`../`, an absolute path, a wrong-length string) — the only way such a value can reach them, since `put()` computes the hash itself; and create the data dir inside a world-writable path | The accessor rejects any non-hex hash before touching the filesystem, so resolution can never leave the data directory; `InsecureLocationError` for the unsafe location |
| SEC-10 | FR-CONSOLE-05 | Network | Spoofing / A01 (no authN by design) | Start with `CONSOLE_BIND = 0.0.0.0`; start with `backend_profile = 'cloud-hosted'`; connect from another LAN host | Loopback binding enforced; refusal to start on the cloud profile; the LAN connection is refused at the socket |
| SEC-11 | FR-CONSOLE-17 | Browser | Information disclosure / A01 | Exercise review, blind and student views, then inspect browser storage and caches | Nothing written; no service worker |
| SEC-12 | FR-CONSOLE-18 | Browser | Supply chain / A08 | Record all network requests during a full console session | Zero requests to any origin but its own |
| SEC-13 | FR-STORE-07, FR-STORE-12 | Data at rest | Information disclosure / retention | Purge a cohort, then scan raw file bytes and the blob directory; inspect Tier D for name-mapped columns | Student text unrecoverable from file bytes; Tier D pseudonymized |
| SEC-14 | — | Supply chain | A06 vulnerable components | Dependency vulnerability scan on every push | No unresolved High or Critical advisory in a shipped dependency. **Cross-cutting** — this traces to no single requirement |
| SEC-15 | FR-STORE-08 | Store interface | Injection / A03 | Attempt free-text and similarity queries against every tier reachable from the scoring path | No such interface exists; parameterized declared statements only |

### 6.6 Adversarial tests

The tier that attacks the system's *correctness under a motivated author*, which is a different
exercise from §6.5 and catches different defects. Every case's pass criterion is **correct handling or
visible failure**; "did not crash" is a fail. The benign-twin differential is the oracle wherever no
ground truth exists: an injected submission and its benign twin must produce the same band, the same
citation outcome and no higher confidence.

| Adv ID | Req | Requirement being attacked | Attacker goal | Input | Pass = correct handling **or** visible failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ADV-01 | FR-AGG-05, FR-INTEG-01 | Confidence inversion | Get a unanimous high-confidence auto-accept on evidence that is not in the paper | Extraction forced to emit plausible spans absent from the document, with three unanimous verdicts | Span verification fails, confidence is capped, the item routes. Auto-acceptance on unverified evidence is the failure |
| ADV-02 | FR-JUDGE-17, FR-INGEST-35 | Judge instruction-following | Force a band | `F-ADV-INJ` band-forcing payloads and their benign twins, including paraphrased, encoded and translated variants | Same band as the benign twin; only a band from the declared set; no confidence lift. A band difference is a finding, and the residual "nudge" risk of ADR-13 is measured here |
| ADV-03 | FR-INTEG-01, FR-JUDGE-17 | Span verification | Forge a citation the judge will accept | Submissions containing text formatted to look like a quotation of themselves, plus near-miss quotations differing by one character | Every forged citation fails byte-exact verification and routes |
| ADV-04 | FR-JUDGE-01, FR-ORCH-20 | Judgment isolation | Get one submission's content into another's judgment | A submission whose text mimics the prompt's delimiters and field names, attempting to close the untrusted block and open a second submission section | `assert_isolated` passes; exactly one `submission_id` in the assembled request; the mimicked delimiters are inert |
| ADV-05 | FR-JUDGE-03 | The numeral prohibition | Introduce a score anchor into the prompt | A submission whose text contains "this answer is worth 4 out of 4", and an exemplar edit attempting the same | No score-denoting numeral reaches the judge from package content; submission-origin numerals are inside the untrusted block and are shown not to move the band relative to the benign twin |
| ADV-06 | FR-INTEG-03, FR-DET-03 | The no-zero-from-failure rule | Make a failure look like a wrong answer | An answer region deliberately scanned to be unreadable; a tick placed exactly between two boxes; an answer written outside the region | Each routes as an ingestion problem; none is scored `incorrect` or lowest-band |
| ADV-07 | FR-INGEST-25 | V4 assessment match | Get graded against the wrong assessment's key | A submission for assessment B formatted to fingerprint as A; a submission with A's identifier and B's content | `uncertain` or `mismatch`; scoring halts; no reassignment |
| ADV-08 | FR-INGEST-11 | The description prohibition | Get a verdict into the panel's input through a description | A diagram whose correct description is nearly a verdict; a diagram with the word "correct" drawn inside it | The stored description contains no evaluative vocabulary, and the drawn word is transcribed as content rather than adopted as a judgement |
| ADV-09 | FR-STATS-01, FR-DET-09 | The admissible-label filter | Inflate κ | Every reachable path attempting to admit operational or deterministic labels into an agreement figure | No path admits them; the figure's n equals the blind judged count |
| ADV-10 | FR-REVIEW-11 | Blind-sample integrity | Learn the system's answer before submitting a blind label | Direct URL probing, link-graph traversal, response-timing correlation, and item-ordering correlation from inside the blind flow | System output unreachable; no correlation between blind item order and stored confidence |
| ADV-11 | FR-SYNTH-03 | The score-claim prohibition | Get a score into the narrative | Verdicts engineered to elicit "one of the strongest answers in the class" and similar paraphrases | Pattern-matched claims are rejected. **Paraphrases will get through** — this is §2.3 Q-06 and the case measures the rate rather than asserting zero |
| ADV-12 | FR-AGG-08, FR-ORCH-11 | Routing policy | Make a wrong answer look certain, so review budget is spent elsewhere | Submissions engineered to be fluent, well-structured and confidently wrong, mid-band, with clean OCR | The random arm samples them independently of confidence, so a systematically mis-routed population is still detectable in the blind and random-arm labels |

### 6.7 Fuzz and property-based tests

| ID | Req | Target | Generator / corpus | Invariant or crash criterion | Examples per run | Seed policy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FUZZ-01 | FR-INGEST-33, FR-INGEST-34 | The PDF ingestion path | Structure-aware PDF generator seeded with `F-ADV-PDF` and every bug-triggering input ever found; corpus committed to the repo | No crash, no hang past the wall-clock ceiling, no unhandled exception outside the declared taxonomy; every outcome is a successful ingest or a quarantine; memory bounded | 200 in CI, 30-minute campaign nightly | Seed recorded on every failure; a failing seed is committed to the corpus permanently |
| FUZZ-02 | FR-INGEST-02, FR-INGEST-16 | Markdown assembly and region emission | Generated page sequences with duplicates, gaps, mixed orientations and mixed encodings | Region offsets always address inside `document.markdown`; `content_state` always one of the three declared values; assembly is deterministic under input reordering when an order source exists | 200 / nightly campaign | As above |
| FUZZ-03 | FR-INTEG-01, FR-EXTRACT-01 | `verify_span` and span emission | Generated documents (ASCII, multi-byte UTF-8, CRLF, empty) crossed with generated spans (in-bounds, out-of-bounds, negative, inverted, mid-codepoint) | `verify_span` returns a bool for every input and never raises; it is `True` exactly when the bytes match and the span is in bounds | 1,000 in CI | Fixed seed set in CI; random nightly |
| FUZZ-04 | FR-JUDGE-09, FR-JUDGE-04 | The model-response parser | Generated JSON: valid; field-permuted; missing fields; extra fields; wrong types; truncated mid-token; deeply nested; enormous strings | Parsing either yields a valid `ScoringResult` or raises `MalformedResponseError`; never any other exception; a permuted field order is always a contract violation | 1,000 in CI | Fixed seed set |
| FUZZ-05 | FR-AGG-01, FR-AGG-02, FR-GRADE-02 | Aggregation and policy application | Generated band sets (2, 4, 6 bands; arbitrary non-decreasing point tables including negatives), verdict lists of odd length, and closed-vocabulary policies | Aggregated points always equal `points_for_band(median_band)`; totals never exceed the maximum achievable; policy application is order-independent over criteria; no even panel is ever aggregated | 1,000 in CI | Fixed seed set |
| FUZZ-06 | FR-PKG-05, FR-ORCH-01 | Dependency graphs and work-ID derivation | Generated criterion graphs up to 30 nodes, cyclic and acyclic; generated work-ID input tuples | Cycles always rejected; `topological_order` always satisfies every edge; distinct input tuples always yield distinct `work_id`s | 500 in CI | Fixed seed set |
| FUZZ-07 | FR-STORE-06, FR-STORE-04 | Blob store and the write queue | Generated byte strings; generated interleavings of result and status writes | `get(put(b)) == b`; `path()` always resolves inside the data directory; the result-plus-status atomicity invariant holds for every interleaving | 500 in CI | Fixed seed set |

### 6.8 Resilience and failure injection

The design's error-handling sections are a page of promises. This tier tests them, one case per
promise, asserting the **specific** promised behaviour rather than "it recovered".

| ID | Req | Injected failure | Where | Promised behavior (design ref) | Assertion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RES-01 | FR-STORE-10 | Disk full (`ENOSPC`) | Mid-batch write | Halt after committing outstanding ledger status transitions (§9.11) | No result row without its status transition; the process halts; the ledger is resumable |
| RES-02 | FR-STORE-09 | Permission denied on the data directory | At open | Refuse to start | `InsecureLocationError` or a permission error at startup; no partial initialization |
| RES-03 | NFR-STORE-02 | `SIGKILL` during a commit | Writer thread | Recover to the last committed batch, lose at most 5 s | Twenty randomized repetitions; no corruption; bounded loss |
| RES-04 | FR-ORCH-02, NFR-ORCH-02 | `SIGKILL` mid-Sweep-1 with leases outstanding | Orchestrator | Resume with no duplicated and no lost work (§9.10) | Result set identical to the uninterrupted baseline |
| RES-05 | FR-ORCH-02 | `SIGKILL` between Sweep 1 and Sweep 2 | Orchestrator | As above | As above |
| RES-06 | FR-ORCH-09 | `SIGKILL` after a verdict is written but before its escalation units are leased | Orchestrator | The escalation was written in the same transaction, so it survives (§9.10) | The escalation units exist after resume |
| RES-07 | FR-ORCH-02 | `SIGKILL` during synthesis | Orchestrator | Resume; a retried synthesis unit conflicts rather than duplicating (ADR-8) | No duplicate `narrative` rows |
| RES-08 | FR-ORCH-26, FR-AGG-12 | A judge call failing permanently, leaving two verdicts | Sweep 2 | Retry for the third; then discard the second and fall back to single-judge provisional; never adjudicate between two (§9.11) | Exact final state; no two-judge aggregation anywhere |
| RES-09 | FR-PROV-08, FR-ORCH-16 | Model server unreachable | Provider | Backoff, then pause the run on the same backend; do not fail units (§9.11) | Units are not failed; the run pauses; resume binds the same backend |
| RES-10 | FR-PROV-05, FR-ORCH-17 | Served build changes mid-run | Provider | Pause and alert (§9.11) | `BuildChangedError`; run paused; alert emitted |
| RES-11 | FR-PROV-07 | Sustained HTTP 429 | Provider | Expected, not an error: honour `Retry-After`, back off, reduce concurrency (§9.13) | No unit failed; concurrency reduced; `rate_limited_calls` incremented |
| RES-12 | FR-ORCH-18, NFR-JUDGE-05 | Malformed model output, persistently | Sweep 2 | Three retries then quarantine the unit; the run continues (§9.11) | Exact attempt count; unit quarantined; no default band written |
| RES-13 | FR-ORCH-19 | Out-of-memory during a model swap | `edge-local` orchestration | Reduce concurrency, retry, then drop to a smaller panel and **record it in `panel_config`** (§9.11) | The reduced panel is recorded, so a later validation record cannot claim the full panel |
| RES-14 | FR-STORE-11 | Wall clock jumps backwards ten minutes | Lease accounting | An expired lease never appears live (§9.11) | Exact expiry from the monotonic counter |
| RES-15 | FR-ORCH-04 | A worker stops heartbeating | Lease sweeper | The lease expires and the unit returns to `pending` | Exact transition at the lease boundary and not before |
| RES-16 | FR-CONSOLE-01, NFR-CONSOLE-03 | The console process killed mid-run | Console | No run depends on a browser session; control rows queue and are picked up on next start | The run completes; queued control rows apply |
| RES-17 | NFR-SYS-01 | No network interface available on the host | Whole pipeline | The full pipeline runs to completion (`edge-local`) | An end-to-end run completes on E5 with networking disabled |
| RES-18 | NFR-SYS-02 | Process restart after an uncontrolled kill | Whole pipeline | RPO ≤ 5 s of completed work; RTO ≤ 1 minute to resume | Measured on E1 and confirmed once on E4 during `PERF-10` |

### 6.9 Regression and baselines

**Policy.** Every defect fixed gains a test that **fails against the unfixed code and passes after**,
written before the fix wherever practical — a test never observed failing is a test not known to work.
The test is named after the defect so its purpose survives the person who wrote it. Per this repo's
`CLAUDE.md`, a defect fix with no existing `TC-*` coverage gets its regression test written inline and
the case added to this plan in the same PR; a test in the repo but not in this plan makes the plan lie
about its coverage.

**Baseline artifacts and who reviews a change to them.** Snapshot testing degrades into "regenerate
until green" unless the reviewer and the grounds are named, so:

| ID | Req | Baseline | Reviewer and grounds for accepting a diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-REG-01 | FR-INGEST-04, FR-INGEST-06 | Canonical assembled Markdown per `F-SYNTH` and `F-GRAPHIC` document | The ingestion owner. Accepted only alongside a deliberate transcription-prompt version bump or a stated assembly-rule change; never "the model changed its mind" |
| TC-REG-02 | FR-PKG-10 | The exported package archive for the reference package | The package owner. Accepted only with a schema-version bump or a declared export-format change |
| TC-REG-03 | FR-GRADE-17 | The CSV and per-student PDF exports | The grading owner. Accepted only with a declared export-mapping change; a diff in a *mark* is a defect, not a baseline update |
| TC-REG-04 | FR-CONSOLE-13, FR-CONSOLE-15 | Rendered HTML of the review queue, the rollup and the student view | The console owner. Accepted for deliberate layout changes; **never** for a change that removes a §11.6 invariant's rendered element |
| TC-REG-05 | FR-CONFORM-01, FR-CONFORM-08 | Per-criterion score distributions of `F-FROZEN` on each backend | The whole team, at release. A shift with an unchanged package is build substitution (`FR-CONFORM-08`), not a baseline to update |
| TC-REG-06 | FR-ORCH-01 | The `work_id` reference values | Nobody may accept a diff casually: a changed `work_id` means every stored result for that shape is now unreachable. Requires an explicit migration note |

**Permanent contract baselines.** Separate from the artifact baselines above, because they are not
snapshots and **no diff to them is ever acceptable**: each is a named regression entry for one of the
18 safety-property clauses of design §4.7, kept permanently and release-gating per §4.8 item 11. A
failure is a design conversation and an ADR, never a baseline update (§4.10).

| Regression entry | Clause | Case | What its failure means |
|---|---|---|---|
| REG-CT-CONF-14 | CT-CONF-14 | TC-CONF-C14 | An existing run's backend, panel or ceilings became changeable |
| REG-CT-PROV-15 | CT-PROV-15 | TC-PROV-C15 | Egress exists outside the single seam |
| REG-CT-STORE-08 | CT-STORE-08 | TC-STORE-C08 | A cross-student contamination channel is reachable from the scoring path |
| REG-CT-INGEST-09 | CT-INGEST-09 | TC-INGEST-C09 | A gate outcome can become a score |
| REG-CT-INGEST-13 | CT-INGEST-13 | TC-INGEST-C13 | Unneutralized content can reach a model, or a failure resolves to processing |
| REG-CT-EXTRACT-08 | CT-EXTRACT-08 | TC-EXTRACT-C08 | A failed extraction is indistinguishable from a blank answer |
| REG-CT-INTEG-03 | CT-INTEG-03 | TC-INTEG-C03 | An integrity signal fails open |
| REG-CT-INTEG-05 | CT-INTEG-05 | TC-INTEG-C05 | The detection path shares code with the path it certifies |
| REG-CT-INTEG-07 | CT-INTEG-07 | TC-INTEG-C07 | Absent evidence can become a lowest-band verdict |
| REG-CT-JUDGE-02 | CT-JUDGE-02 | TC-JUDGE-C02 | The scoring request is no longer a closed whitelist |
| REG-CT-JUDGE-03 | CT-JUDGE-03 | TC-JUDGE-C03 | A numeral, a second submission, or prior history reached a judge |
| REG-CT-DET-03 | CT-DET-03 | TC-DET-C03 | A scanning failure became a wrong answer |
| REG-CT-AGG-05 | CT-AGG-05 | TC-AGG-C05 | Panel unanimity can outrun adverse evidence — the confidence inversion is gone |
| REG-CT-GRADE-07 | CT-GRADE-07 | TC-GRADE-C07 | Something was imputed into a delivered grade |
| REG-CT-REVIEW-08 | CT-REVIEW-08 | TC-REVIEW-C08 | An operational label can enter a validity statistic |
| REG-CT-REVIEW-09 | CT-REVIEW-09 | TC-REVIEW-C09 | System output is reachable from the blind flow |
| REG-CT-STATS-01 | CT-STATS-01 | TC-STATS-C01 | Agreement is computable over an inadmissible population |
| REG-CT-STATS-03 | CT-STATS-03 | TC-STATS-C03 | Absence of evidence can render as a number |

Three further entries are kept permanently on the same terms although their clauses are not on §4.7's
safety list, because each guards a Critical risk in this plan's own register: **REG-CT-STORE-02**
(`CT-STORE-02`, RISK-31 — write asynchrony), **REG-CT-ORCH-06** (`CT-ORCH-06`, RISK-02 — one
submission per request), and **REG-CT-PKG-07** (`CT-PKG-07`, RISK-08 — `NoValidationData` at the
catalog boundary, the counterpart to REG-CT-STATS-03).

**Baseline suite.** `TC-E2E-02`'s full result set is the standing regression baseline for the pipeline:
340-odd grades, their coverage records, their routing decisions and their confidence values, compared
after every change to any scoring-path module.

### 6.10 Observability tests

The design promises specific counters and specific alerts. Untested telemetry breaks silently and is
discovered during the incident it was meant to prevent — and for RISK-23 the metric is the *only*
signal there is.

| ID | Req | Promised signal | Trigger | Assertion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OBS-01 | FR-INGEST-29 | `ocr_failure_rate` and unresolved-mark rate **recorded separately**; pages with text layer; mean and max `text_layer_divergence`; per-gate pass/fail counts; quarantine count by gate; description second-pass disagreement rate | A full cohort ingest with mixed outcomes | Every field present and correctly typed; the two rates are separate fields, since they have different remedies |
| OBS-02 | FR-STORE-05 | Write-queue depth, batch commit latency, database file sizes, free disk space, `VACUUM` duration | A saturated run | Present and correct; the free-disk alert fires against a synthetic breach of the projected remaining-run requirement |
| OBS-03 | FR-ORCH-23 | `run_metrics` in full: total and escalated units, quarantined units, wall clock, tokens, `cache_hit_rate`, peak concurrency, retries, rate-limit counters, estimated and actual cost, resolved builds, model swap count and duration | A run with quarantines, escalations and a swap | Every field present; each matches a hand-counted expectation |
| OBS-04 | FR-PROV-12, NFR-JUDGE-01 | `cache_hit_rate` | A run with prompt ordering deliberately broken so the prefix is no longer invariant | The rate collapses **and the alert fires**. This is the only detection path for RISK-23, where the symptom is a fivefold slowdown with no error |
| OBS-05 | FR-ORCH-14, FR-ORCH-15 | Alerts: escalation rate above budget; a criterion tripping the breaker; cost within 10% of ceiling; `cache_hit_rate` collapse; a run paused for any reason | Synthetic breach of each condition, one at a time | Each alert fires on its own condition and does not fire on the others |
| OBS-06 | FR-INTEG-08 | Span-verification failure rate, empty-evidence rate, `ocr_overlap_risk` rate, described-evidence rate, sufficiency-flag rate, extractor-disagreement rate | A run with hallucinated spans injected at a known rate | Rates match the injected rate; the verification-failure alert fires above threshold |
| OBS-07 | FR-JUDGE-11, FR-AGG-11 | Per criterion and judge: uncited rate, insufficiency rate, band histogram, contract-violation rate, latency, prefix hit rate. Per criterion: `band_spread` distribution, ordinal α, escalation rate, auto-accept rate, and the count of each hard cap fired | A run with injected contract violations on one judge and integrity caps firing on one criterion | Both alerts fire: violations concentrated on one judge, and caps firing at an unusual rate on one criterion |
| OBS-08 | FR-DET-07 | Per question: correct rate, blank count, unresolved count, most-chosen distractor | A cohort with an elevated unresolved count | The alert fires and is labelled a **scanning** problem; it is never presented as item difficulty |
| OBS-09 | FR-GRADE-04, FR-STATS-11 | Grades by state, `boundary_at_risk` count, coverage distribution, finalization path taken, amendment count; label counts by type and origin; blind coverage per administration | A run finishing with outstanding `incomplete` grades, after two administrations with the blind sample skipped | Both alerts fire: outstanding `incomplete` grades past the window, and the validation record no longer advancing |
| OBS-10 | FR-CONF-09, NFR-SYS-11 | One structured log line per run start containing `profile_summary()`; the profile recorded in the audit record behind every grade | Any run start | Emitted exactly once, credential-free, and byte-identical to what the audit record stores |
| OBS-11 | FR-REVIEW-16, FR-CONSOLE-06 | `review_minutes_used`, items shown versus flagged, override rate by criterion, group-action share, blind completion rate, mean versus estimated seconds; skip rates per optional setup step | A full review session and a full setup | Present and correct. The skip rates are the pilot's actual instrument for HLD §11.9, so their absence is a requirement failure, not a nicety |

### 6.11 Contract suites — the `CT-*` clause cases

**This is the regression spine of the plan.** §5 argues that each module does its job; this section
argues that each module is still safe to depend on. Every one of the design's 330 `CT-*` clauses gets
at least one case here, named `TC-<MODULE>-C<nn>` for `CT-<MODULE>-nn`, so a failing test name points
straight at the broken promise. The policy behind the section — who owns each suite, how doubles are
held to it, and what a red result means — is §4.10, and it is worth reading before this section rather
than after.

**How to read a row.** The columns are the same fields the §5 blocks carry, compressed to one line:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Case** | `TC-<MODULE>-C<nn>`, one-to-one with the clause. Stable — it is the name that appears in CI output |
| **Clause / Kind** | The clause verified, and its design-assigned kind, which is what fixes the technique (§4.10, and `references/test-design-techniques.md` §13) |
| **The violation it catches** | This is the **`Breaks if`** field. The concrete thing the case does and asserts, written as *what would turn it red*, not as a restatement of the clause — a row that only restated the clause would be a title, not a test. For the 18 safety properties the field is expanded into a named **adversarial construction**: an actual change someone might propose, asserted to turn the case red while every functional case stays green |
| **Rung** | §4.2 isolation: **0** doubles/pure · **1** in-memory fakes · **2** real dependency · **3** real neighbours · **4** full system |
| **Oracle** | Exact value, invariant, differential, golden, or artifact assertion |
| **Pri** | P0 release-gating · P1 must pass before the phase ships · P2 should pass |

**The discriminator, applied to every row.** *Would this case go red if the clause broke while every
`FR-*` case stayed green?* Rows that failed that question were rewritten until they passed it. Where a
clause shares its central assertion with a §5 case, the row says so — and the row stays, because the
two run at different times, against different implementations, for different reasons (§4.10).

**Full block form** is used for the eighteen safety-property clauses of design §4.7 and for the
non-promise clauses. Both need more than a row: a safety property needs its adversarial construction
("a plausible refactor that breaks this while every functional case stays green"), and a non-promise
needs a consumer sweep rather than a single assertion.

**What replaced the old `CS-*` rows.** Plan v1.0 carried a seven-row ad-hoc contract table covering
`M-PROV` and `M-STORE` only, written before the design had a contract scheme. Those rows are
superseded by the clause suites below — the six provider rows by §6.11.2 and the store row by
§6.11.3, both of which are strictly wider — and the `CS-*` IDs are **retired**, with every reference
to them in §4.2, §4.3, §5 and §7.1 repointed to the clause case that now carries the assertion. Their
compatibility prose survives, generalized, in §4.10. §8.2's `TS-00` and `TS-06` are repointed too.

---

#### 6.11.1 `M-CONF` — 14 clauses, consumed by 7 modules

A pure, tiny module that is the enforcement point for two Critical risks (RISK-10 credential and
consent leakage, RISK-22 backend rebinding). Purity makes the whole suite rung 0 and cheap, so there
is no reason to sample rather than enumerate. `CT-CONF-14` is a safety property **and** a non-promise
and gets block form below.

| Case | Clause | Kind | What the case does, and the violation it catches | Rung | Oracle | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-CONF-C01 | CT-CONF-01 | surface | Call both entry points with a socket-blocking guard and an open-file audit hook installed; assert neither dispatches, and that both return a value rather than a coroutine. Catches the day someone makes resolution `async` to fetch a remote profile — a change no `FR-*` case notices because the result is still correct. | 0 | Artifact assertion (no socket, no unnamed file) plus a `not asyncio.iscoroutinefunction` check | P1 |
| TC-CONF-C02 | CT-CONF-02 | data | Enumerate `RunConfig` fields against the design's Interfaces list; assert exact set equality, not a subset. Then sweep the two iff-conditions: `hardware_profile` non-null **iff** `edge-local`, `cost_ceiling`/`cost_currency` non-null **iff** `cloud-hosted`/`dev-ci`, `retention_setting` non-null for `cloud-hosted`. Both directions, because only asserting one lets a stray non-null through. Panel length in `{1,3,5}` with `2` and `4` and `0` each asserted to raise. | 0 | Exact value; set equality on the field list | P0 |
| TC-CONF-C03 | CT-CONF-03 | data | For every `ModelRef` reachable from a resolved `RunConfig`, assert `is_resolved()`; then assert per backend what resolution *means* — weights path + quantization + hash for `edge-local`, provider-pinned slug otherwise. A ref carrying a floating tag (`:latest`) must fail. Catches a `build_id` that stops being sufficient to identify what answered, which is what every validation record is keyed on. | 0 | Invariant over the reachable ref set | P0 |
| TC-CONF-C04 | CT-CONF-04 | behaviour | Attempt attribute assignment on every public field, assert `TypeError` each time. Then enumerate the public surface and assert no member returns a copy with a different `backend_profile` or `panel`. Catches a `with_backend()` convenience helper — the exact change that makes RISK-22 possible again. | 0 | Exact exception type; artifact assertion over the member list | P0 |
| TC-CONF-C05 | CT-CONF-05 | behaviour | Purity: call `resolve_run_config(cfg, cohort)` twice with identical inputs under a mutated process environment between calls (different `HARNESS_*` values, different cwd, different clock); assert both results equal field-for-field **including `panel_build_ref`**. Catches the environment leaking in past the snapshot. | 0 | Differential — result equality across a perturbed environment | P0 |
| TC-CONF-C06 | CT-CONF-06 | behaviour | Round-trip: resolve, serialize to a `run` row, rehydrate, assert field-for-field equality. Then perturb the current configuration (different backend, different resolved build, different panel order) and assert `BackendMismatchError` rather than a quietly-resolved config. Shares its central assertion with `TC-CONF-04`, and stays because it must run on every `M-CONF` change. | 0 | Exact value on the round trip; exact exception on each perturbation | P0 |
| TC-CONF-C07 | CT-CONF-07 | data | Compute `panel_build_ref` for the same ordered panel in two processes on two working directories; assert equality. Then assert inequality under each of: one member swapped, one member's quantization changed, the same members in a different order. Ordering is the one most likely to be "optimized" into a sorted set, which would silently merge two distinct panels under one key. | 0 | Differential across processes; exact inequality per perturbation | P0 |
| TC-CONF-C08 | CT-CONF-08 | error | One case per named error — `ConfigurationError`, `UnresolvedModelRefError`, `BackendMismatchError`, `ConsentGateError`. For each: provoke it, assert the exact type, assert it is **not** retryable, and assert **no `run` row exists afterwards**. The third assertion is the one that catches a partial write and the one usually skipped. | 0 | Exact exception type; state assertion over the store | P0 |
| TC-CONF-C09 | CT-CONF-09 | state | Run a full resolution with the data directory, the blob directory and the database under a write-audit hook; assert **zero** writes of any kind. The negative half is the case: a module that "helpfully" caches its resolution to disk has broken the clause while every functional test passes. | 2 | Artifact assertion — an empty write log | P1 |
| TC-CONF-C10 | CT-CONF-10 | security | Seed a credential with a distinctive sentinel value into every source the module reads. Assert the sentinel appears in **no** `to_persisted_dict()` output, **no** `profile_summary()`, **no** exception message from any of the four errors above, and **no** emitted log line. Assert over the artifacts, never over intent. | 0 | Artifact assertion — sentinel scan across four surfaces | P0 |
| TC-CONF-C11 | CT-CONF-11 | config | For each of the six `HARNESS_*` keys: assert the documented default (`HARNESS_ALLOW_REMOTE_REAL_WORK` defaults false), and assert the externally-visible behaviour change when it moves. Then the negative that matters: with **no** key set, assert resolution **raises** rather than selecting a backend. A silent default here selects a grader by accident. | 0 | Exact value per key; exact exception on absence | P0 |
| TC-CONF-C12 | CT-CONF-12 | perf | Assert resolution completes under 50 ms on the reference environment, as a threshold, **and** that it performs no model call, no network call and no database read. The second half is the durable one: the latency figure could be met by a warm cache that still reads the database, which would break `M-CONSOLE`'s right to resolve on the request path. A loosened bound must edit this number in review (RISK-33). | 0 | Threshold at the stated environment; artifact assertion on I/O | P1 |
| TC-CONF-C13 | CT-CONF-13 | observe | Assert exactly one structured log line per run start, containing `profile_summary()` — and assert the module emits **no metric of its own**. Both halves are contract: the "nothing else" is what stops this module growing a telemetry surface that ops then depends on. | 0 | Artifact assertion over captured log output | P2 |
| TC-CONF-C14 | CT-CONF-14 | behaviour | **Non-promise, and a safety property.** Block form below. | 0 / 3 | — | P0 |

**TC-CONF-C14 — no operation changes an existing run's backend, panel, or ceilings**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Clause | `CT-CONF-14` (behaviour, non-promise) — safety property per design §4.7 |
| Guards | RISK-22, RISK-10; HLD `R1` |
| Consumers | `M-ORCH`, `M-CONSOLE` |
| Level / type | Contract, negative, adversarial |
| Isolation | Rung 0 for the surface sweep; rung 3 for the consumer sweep |
| Priority | P0 |

**Steps**:
1. Enumerate every public member of `RunConfig` and of the module, by reflection. Assert none of them
   accepts a `backend_profile`, `panel`, `cost_ceiling` or `retention_setting` argument on an object
   that already exists — the assertion is over the *surface*, not over a call, so a method that exists
   but is never called still fails.
2. Attempt the mutation through each plausible back door: attribute assignment, `dataclasses.replace`,
   `__setstate__`, `copy` with an override, and rehydration from a hand-edited `run` row.
3. Consumer sweep at rung 3: with `M-ORCH` and `M-CONSOLE` real, assert neither exposes a path that
   reaches a rebinding — a console control that "restarts with a different backend" must create a new
   run with a new id, and the case asserts the id changed.

**Oracle**: artifact assertion over the reflected member list; exact exception type per back door;
exact inequality on `run_id` in step 3.

**Adversarial construction** (the case that makes this a safety property rather than a preference):
implement `RunConfig.with_backend(profile)` returning a copy, and wire `M-CONSOLE`'s retry control to
it. Assert that **this construction turns TC-CONF-C14 red while every `FR-CONF-*` case in §5 stays
green**. If it does not, the case is testing something adjacent to the clause and must be tightened.

**Regression**: `REG-CT-CONF-14`, kept permanently in the baseline set of §6.9.

**Automatable**: yes — `tests/contract/conf/test_no_rebinding.py`

#### 6.11.2 `M-PROV` — 16 clauses, consumed by 8 modules

**The suite this plan depends on most.** RISK-37: almost every case in this document runs against
`RecordedFixtureProvider`, so if the double drifts from the contract the live providers keep, the fast
tier stays green while describing a system that does not exist. The whole of §6.11.2 is therefore
**parametrized over `[RecordedFixtureProvider, LocalServerProvider, OpenRouterProvider]`** — the same
cases, three implementations, per §4.10. The fixture run is fast-tier; the two live runs are nightly
under the `live` marker, and **their failure is P0, not advisory**, because they are the only thing
that can detect drift.

`CT-PROV-15` is a safety property and `CT-PROV-16` a non-promise; both get block form.

| Case | Clause | Kind | What the case does, and the violation it catches | Rung | Oracle | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-PROV-C01 | CT-PROV-01 | surface | Assert `complete` is synchronous and blocking (not a coroutine, returns after the call completes), that one call produces exactly one model call, and that `capabilities`/`estimate_cost`/`verify_retention` make **no** model call. Then the ownership half: assert the module starts no thread and owns no queue, by counting threads across a batch of calls. Catches an internal batching or worker-pool "optimization" that would break the caller's ownership of concurrency — and would break `M-JUDGE`'s isolation with it. | 2 | Artifact assertion — call counter and thread census | P0 |
| TC-PROV-C02 | CT-PROV-02 | behaviour | The parametrization itself, asserted rather than assumed: run the entire `CT-PROV` suite against all three implementations from one `RunConfig`-only difference, and assert no case needs an implementation-specific branch. A test that skips on a backend is a contract violation and fails the case. | 2 / live | Differential across three implementations | P0 |
| TC-PROV-C03 | CT-PROV-03 | data | One assertion per `Completion` field for presence and type. Then the distinctions the clause insists on: `cost` is the **only** nullable field, and null **only** on `edge-local` and fixture — a `cost` of `0.0` on a cloud call must fail, because *not measured* and *measured zero* are different facts. `resolved_build` is asserted **unequal** to the requested ref in a substitution fixture, which is the assertion that catches the field silently echoing the request. `text` byte-identical to the wire payload, unparsed. | 2 / live | Exact value per field; differential on `resolved_build` | P0 |
| TC-PROV-C04 | CT-PROV-04 | data | Assert `Capabilities` is declared, not discovered: call it with the transport hard-blocked and assert it still answers. Assert stability across a run by sampling at start and end. Then the semantic assertion that matters — `deterministic_at_temperature_zero` is a **claim**, so the case asserts the field is *not* derived from any measurement, and that `M-STATS`'s measured reality disagreeing with it is not an error here. | 0 | Artifact assertion; exact value | P1 |
| TC-PROV-C05 | CT-PROV-05 | behaviour | Capture the assembled payload at the caller and the payload on the wire; assert **byte identity**. Sweep the mutations that would pass a looser check: a field added, keys reordered, whitespace normalized, a template applied, unicode renormalized. Each must fail the case. This is what keeps `M-JUDGE`'s byte-identical prefix identical on the wire, so a violation costs 5× wall clock (RISK-23) with no error. | 2 / live | Byte-level differential | P0 |
| TC-PROV-C06 | CT-PROV-06 | behaviour | Retry **only** on transport failure, timeout, 429, 5xx, or structural parse failure. The decisive negative: a response that **parsed successfully** is never re-requested — assert the call count is exactly 1 across a sweep of semantically odd but structurally valid responses (empty text, refusal, a verdict the caller dislikes). Then enumerate the module surface and assert **no parameter, flag or code path** exists that could enable resampling. "One judgment, one sample" is a property callers build on; a `retry_if` hook would destroy it invisibly. | 0 | Exact call count; artifact assertion over the surface | P0 |
| TC-PROV-C07 | CT-PROV-07 | error | One case per named error — `TransportError`, `RateLimitedError`, `MalformedResponseError`, `ProviderUnavailableError`, `BuildChangedError`, `FixtureMissingError`. For each: provoke it, assert the exact type, assert **the retryability the clause claims** (first two retried internally before surfacing; last three never retried), and assert the state left behind — nothing written, only tokens consumed. Retryability is one of the two most-missed breaking changes (RISK-34), so it is asserted explicitly per error rather than inferred from behaviour. | 0 | Exact type; exact internal-attempt count; state assertion | P0 |
| TC-PROV-C08 | CT-PROV-08 | behaviour | Induce `ProviderUnavailableError` on one panel member and assert **no substitution occurs on any code path** — no other model answers, no degraded mode, no cached response served. Enumerate configuration for a fallback knob and assert none exists. Catches a well-meant "resilience" feature that would silently let a different instrument grade half a cohort (HLD `R1`). | 0 | Exact exception; artifact assertion that no alternate build answered | P0 |
| TC-PROV-C09 | CT-PROV-09 | behaviour | Purity of `estimate_cost(plan)`: same plan, same declared costs, same answer, with the transport blocked — assert it never dispatches. Then monotonicity: read `actual_cost` at many points through a run, assert non-decreasing, and assert it is readable **at any time** including mid-flight and after a failed call. A cost figure that resets or decreases breaks `M-ORCH`'s ceiling enforcement (RISK-25). | 0 | Exact value; monotonic invariant over a sampled sequence | P1 |
| TC-PROV-C10 | CT-PROV-10 | behaviour | Hermeticity. Key the fixture by a hash of the **fully assembled request**, then assert an unknown request raises `FixtureMissingError` rather than falling through to the network — with the socket layer left open, so a fall-through would actually succeed if the guard were missing. This case is what makes the whole fast tier trustworthy: without it, "no live call in CI" is a hope. | 0 | Exact exception with the transport deliberately available | P0 |
| TC-PROV-C11 | CT-PROV-11 | state | Assert the module writes nothing: full write-audit over database, files and blobs across a batch of calls, expecting an empty log. Then assert the six counters accumulate **in memory** and are read by `M-ORCH` — including the negative that this module never persists them itself, which is what keeps `run_metrics` single-writer (`CT-ORCH-17`). | 2 | Artifact assertion — empty write log; exact counter values | P1 |
| TC-PROV-C12 | CT-PROV-12 | perf | Threshold: under 5 ms of module overhead per call above the provider's own latency, measured against a null transport at the stated environment. Plus the allocation assertion that carries the real meaning — **no per-call copy of the invariant prefix** — so an observed `cache_hit_rate` reflects the caller's ordering, not this module's behaviour. A loosened bound must edit this number in review (RISK-33). | 2 | Threshold; allocation count differential across prefix sizes | P1 |
| TC-PROV-C13 | CT-PROV-13 | security | Sentinel sweep, asserted over artifacts: a distinctive credential value appears in no log line, no exception message and no return value. Request bodies carry `student_ref` and **never** a student name — assert by scanning assembled bodies for a sentinel student name present in the fixture. Then the ordering assertion for `cloud-hosted`: `verify_retention` has confirmed zero-retention routing for **every** panel member **before the first dispatch**, or the run did not start — asserted as a call-order property, because confirming afterwards is the plausible bug. | 2 | Artifact assertion; call-order invariant | P0 |
| TC-PROV-C14 | CT-PROV-14 | observe | Assert the DEBUG per-call fields exist by name (model_ref, resolved build, latency, tokens, retry count) and that the per-run counters are emitted **under the `FR-PROV-12` names**. `cache_hit_rate` is an alert input, so its name and meaning are contract: the case asserts the exact string and that the value is a hit *rate* in `[0,1]`, not a count. Renaming it silently kills RISK-23's only detector. | 2 | Artifact assertion on names; range invariant | P1 |
| TC-PROV-C15 | CT-PROV-15 | security | **Safety property.** Block form below. | 0 | — | P0 |
| TC-PROV-C16 | CT-PROV-16 | behaviour | **Non-promise.** Block form below. | 2 / 3 | — | P0 |

**TC-PROV-C15 — this module is the sole egress point**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Clause | `CT-PROV-15` (security) — safety property per design §4.7 |
| Guards | RISK-10, RISK-29, RISK-32; every consent gate, cost ceiling and air-gap claim in the system |
| Consumers | all modules |
| Level / type | Contract, negative, static analysis plus runtime |
| Isolation | Rung 0 (import graph) and rung 4 (runtime egress) |
| Priority | P0 |

**Steps**:
1. **Static.** An `import-linter` contract (or AST walk) over the whole package: no module other than
   `M-PROV`'s live implementations imports a provider SDK, an HTTP client capable of targeting a model
   endpoint, or any backend-specific symbol. Assert over the *import graph*, not over a grep, so an
   aliased or deferred import inside a function still fails.
2. **Runtime.** Run the full E2E journey at rung 4 with a process-wide socket guard that records every
   outbound connection and the stack that opened it. Assert every recorded connection's stack passes
   through `M-PROV`. Zero exceptions — a health check, a telemetry ping and a font fetch all fail.
3. Assert the audit claim the clause makes on a reviewer's behalf: the set of modules containing any
   egress-capable import has cardinality one.

**Oracle**: artifact assertion over the import graph; artifact assertion over the recorded connection
log. Both are exact — this is a prohibition, so any hit is a failure.

**Adversarial construction**: add a `requests.get` health check to `M-CONSOLE`'s status screen and a
direct SDK import to `M-CONFORM` "to compare raw latencies". Assert **both turn TC-PROV-C15 red while
every `FR-*` case stays green** — including `SEC-03` if that case were scoped only to the scoring
path, which is the gap the runtime half of step 2 closes.

**Regression**: `REG-CT-PROV-15`, permanent. Shares its central assertion with `TC-PROV-05` and
`SEC-03`; it stays separate because it runs on every `M-PROV` change and covers non-scoring paths.

**Automatable**: yes — `tests/contract/prov/test_sole_egress.py`

**TC-PROV-C16 — identical inputs are not promised to produce identical text**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Clause | `CT-PROV-16` (behaviour, **non-promise**) |
| Consumers to sweep | `M-JUDGE`, `M-EXTRACT`, `M-CONFORM` |
| Level / type | Contract, non-promise consumer sweep |
| Isolation | Rung 2 for the provider, rung 3 for each consumer |
| Priority | P0 |

**The technique.** A non-promise is verified by proving **no consumer depends on it** — so the case
does not assert that output varies. It **makes the unpromised thing vary** and asserts every consumer
in the `Consumers` column still behaves correctly.

**Steps**:
1. Configure a provider double that returns *semantically equivalent but textually different* output
   for byte-identical requests: reordered JSON keys, different whitespace, a differently-worded
   rationale, a different but valid citation phrasing.
2. Run `M-JUDGE` at rung 3 across the varying responses. Assert verdicts remain valid and parseable,
   that no code path caches or dedupes on response text, and that no assertion anywhere compares two
   generated strings for equality.
3. Run `M-EXTRACT` the same way; assert span extraction remains correct when the surrounding rationale
   text differs.
4. Run `M-CONFORM`; assert its comparison logic is built on `deterministic_at_temperature_zero`
   (`CT-PROV-04`, the backend's *claim*) and on `M-STATS`'s measurement, never on an assumption of
   textual reproducibility here.
5. Assert no golden file in the repository holds generated text as an exact-match expectation for a
   live tier. Recorded fixtures are exempt by construction — they are keyed by request, not compared
   as output.

**Oracle**: invariant — every consumer produces a correct result under textual variation. Plus an
artifact assertion in step 5.

**Why this is the case nobody writes.** Today, at temperature 0 on one backend, text usually *is*
reproducible. A consumer that quietly depends on it passes every test until a GPU, a driver or a
SQLite version changes — and then fails in the consumer, far from the change. This case is what keeps
that freedom real, and it is the reason `CT-PROV-16` was written down at all.

**Automatable**: yes — `tests/contract/prov/test_nonpromise_determinism.py`

#### 6.11.3 `M-STORE` — 18 clauses, consumed by every module except five

The widest blast radius in the system, and the one place where **§4.10 forbids a double outright**.
Design §3.3 says it plainly: a synchronously-committing in-memory fake hides every `CT-STORE-02`
violation, which is precisely the class of bug this contract exists to catch. The whole suite
therefore runs at **rung 2 against a real temporary SQLite file and a real blob directory**; the
in-memory shortcut permitted by §4.2 is confined to cases touching no write path, and `TC-STORE-C02`
asserts that confinement. `CT-STORE-02` (RISK-31), `CT-STORE-08` (safety property) and `CT-STORE-18`
(non-promise) get block form.

| Case | Clause | Kind | What the case does, and the violation it catches | Rung | Oracle | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-STORE-C01 | CT-STORE-01 | surface | Assert `Store` yields **exactly** three handle kinds — `package(id)`, `cohort(id)`, `durable()` — plus `blobs()` and `purge_cohort(id)`, by set equality on the public surface rather than by presence checks. Then assert a `TierHandle` offers `query`, `enqueue_write`, `transaction` **and nothing else**: an added `execute` or `raw_connection` escape hatch fails the case, because it is the door through which every other clause here gets bypassed. | 2 | Set equality over the reflected surface | P0 |
| TC-STORE-C02 | CT-STORE-02 | behaviour | **Block form below** — the single most load-bearing clause in this contract (RISK-31). | 2 | — | P0 |
| TC-STORE-C03 | CT-STORE-03 | behaviour | Atomicity across tables within one tier handle: write a work unit's result and its ledger transition inside one `transaction()`, kill the process mid-body, reopen, assert **both present or both absent** — never one. Then the negative that is contract: assert cross-tier atomicity is **not** provided, by attempting a transaction spanning two tier handles and asserting it is refused rather than silently splitting. A caller relying on a cross-tier guarantee nobody made is exactly the bug this half prevents. | 2 | State assertion after an uncontrolled kill; exact refusal on the cross-tier attempt | P0 |
| TC-STORE-C04 | CT-STORE-04 | behaviour | Single-writer serialization: drive concurrent writers and readers, assert no reader ever observes a partially applied transaction and no reader blocks the writer. Then the non-promise half — write ordering across different `enqueue_write` calls from different callers is **not** guaranteed except within one `transaction()`. Assert a consumer sweep tolerates reordering (see `TC-STORE-C18`), rather than asserting an order this module never promised. | 2 | Invariant under concurrency; consumer sweep | P0 |
| TC-STORE-C05 | CT-STORE-05 | behaviour | Durability bound as a **threshold**, not a description: kill the process uncontrolled at randomized points under sustained write load; assert at most 100 results **or** 5 seconds of completed work is lost, and that reopening recovers to the last committed batch with no corruption. Both figures are configurable, so the case reads them from configuration and asserts against the configured value — which is what makes a loosened bound (RISK-33) visible as an edit. | 2 | Threshold over repeated kills; integrity check on reopen | P0 |
| TC-STORE-C06 | CT-STORE-06 | behaviour | Drive `enqueue_write` past the configured queue depth; assert it applies backpressure (blocks or slows) **and signals it**. Then the consumer-facing half: assert the signal is distinguishable from a fault, because `CT-STORE-06` requires `M-ORCH` to treat slowness as a reason to reduce dispatch (`FR-ORCH-21`) rather than to quarantine work. A backpressure signal that looks like an error would fail a whole run under load. | 2 | Timing threshold plus exact signal type | P1 |
| TC-STORE-C07 | CT-STORE-07 | surface | `BlobStore.put(data) -> content_hash`: assert content-addressing on SHA-256 against a hand-computed constant, and idempotency — identical bytes yield the same hash and **one** stored copy, asserted by counting files on disk. Then assert `get` and `path` resolve any hash `put` returned for the lifetime of the owning tier, including after a reopen. | 2 | Exact value against a known SHA-256; file count | P1 |
| TC-STORE-C08 | CT-STORE-08 | security | **Safety property.** Block form below. | 2 | — | P0 |

Then the happy path against real files: assert the bytes are gone from disk, not merely unreferenced. It is irreversible and the only operation that deletes student work, so the precondition sweep is exhaustive rather than sampled. | 2 | Exact exception per missing precondition; byte-level file verification | P0 |

| TC-STORE-C18 | CT-STORE-18 | behaviour | **Non-promise.** Block form below. | 2 / 3 | — | P0 |

**TC-STORE-C02 — `enqueue_write` is asynchronous, and callers may not assume otherwise**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Clause | `CT-STORE-02` (behaviour) — design §3.3 calls it "the single most load-bearing clause in this contract and the easiest to get wrong" |
| Guards | RISK-31 |
| Consumers | `M-ORCH`, `M-JUDGE`, `M-EXTRACT`, `M-INGEST`, `M-SYNTH` |
| Level / type | Contract, behaviour, plus a five-consumer sweep |
| Isolation | Rung 2 against a real file; rung 3 for the consumer sweep |
| Priority | P0 |

**Steps**:
1. Call `enqueue_write` and assert it **returns before the row is durable** — verified by reading the
   database from a *separate connection* that cannot see uncommitted state, and asserting the row is
   absent immediately after return. A case asserting only that the row eventually appears would pass
   against a synchronous implementation and is therefore not this case.
2. Assert the two sanctioned ways to observe your own write both work: reading through `transaction()`,
   and waiting for the commit batch.
3. **Consumer sweep at rung 3.** For each of the five consumers, run its real code against a store
   configured with a deliberately *long* commit interval. Any consumer that reads back its own
   `enqueue_write` without going through `transaction()` or awaiting the batch fails here. This is the
   half that catches the bug in the direction it actually occurs.
4. Assert the §4.2 in-memory shortcut is confined: enumerate cases using an in-memory store and assert
   none exercises a write path (§4.10 forbids an in-memory stand-in for this contract).

**Oracle**: exact state from an independent connection at a defined instant; invariant per consumer.

**The failure this prevents, in both directions.** Making it synchronous to fix a flaky test destroys
throughput and lets consumers grow a dependency on read-your-own-write that then breaks when it is
made asynchronous again. Making an already-synchronous path asynchronous silently breaks every caller
that reads its own write. Neither changes a signature; neither fails an `FR-*` case.

**Regression**: `REG-CT-STORE-02`, permanent.

**Automatable**: yes — `tests/contract/store/test_write_asynchrony.py`

**TC-STORE-C08 — no similarity, embedding, or free-text search reachable from the scoring path**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Clause | `CT-STORE-08` (security) — safety property per design §4.7 |
| Guards | RISK-01's cross-student contamination channel; HLD `R15` |
| Consumers | `M-JUDGE`, `M-EXTRACT`, `M-REVIEW` |
| Level / type | Contract, negative, adversarial |
| Isolation | Rung 2 and rung 4 |
| Priority | P0 |

**Steps**:
1. Enumerate the query surface of every tier reachable from the scoring path; assert callers get
   **keyed lookup and declared queries only**. Assert the absence of FTS: no `fts4`/`fts5` virtual
   table, no `MATCH` operator accepted, no vector or embedding column, no `LIKE '%...%'` helper on the
   public surface.
2. Assert the SQLite build itself is exercised without an FTS module reachable through the handle, so
   the prohibition holds structurally and not only by convention.
3. At rung 4, run the E2E journey and assert no query issued during scoring names another student's
   submission — the runtime form of "no cross-student contamination channel".

**Oracle**: artifact assertion over the query surface and over issued statements. Any hit fails.

**Adversarial construction**: add an FTS index over `document_region` to make the review queue's search
box fast — a genuinely attractive feature, since `M-REVIEW` is a listed consumer. Assert this
**turns TC-STORE-C08 red while every `FR-*` case stays green**, which is the whole point: the design
calls this "the structural form of no cross-student contamination channel", and a convenience feature
is exactly how it would come back.

**Regression**: `REG-CT-STORE-08`, permanent.

**Automatable**: yes — `tests/contract/store/test_no_search_surface.py`

**TC-STORE-C18 — no query returns rows in an order this module chose**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Clause | `CT-STORE-18` (behaviour, **non-promise**) |
| Consumers to sweep | all readers — every module except `M-CONF` |
| Level / type | Contract, non-promise consumer sweep |
| Isolation | Rung 2 for the store, rung 3 per consumer |
| Priority | P0 |

**The technique.** Do not assert that order varies. **Make it vary**, and assert every reader still
behaves correctly.

**Steps**:
1. Wrap the store with a shim that deliberately **shuffles** the row order of every `query` result that
   carries no `ORDER BY`, seeded per run so failures reproduce.
2. Run the full suite of every reading module at rung 3 against the shuffling store. Any module whose
   result changes has been depending on incidental order and fails here.
3. Assert the sanctioned escape works: a caller needing an order states it in the statement, and such
   statements are unaffected by the shim.
4. Assert the second non-promise in the same clause: no cross-tier transaction, join, or referential
   integrity. Attempt each and assert refusal — and assert that a Tier R row referencing a Tier P row
   is checked by the owning module, by removing the referent and confirming the *owner* raises, not
   the store.

**Oracle**: differential — each consumer's output under shuffled order must equal its output under
natural order.

**Why it earns its place.** Insertion order is stable in SQLite often enough to be depended on by
accident. The dependency is invisible until a version bump, an index change or a `VACUUM` reorders
pages — and then it fails in `M-GRADE` or `M-REVIEW`, weeks from any change to `M-STORE`. This case is
what makes ADR-6's later move to Postgres survivable, and it is the reason the clause exists.

**Automatable**: yes — `tests/contract/store/test_nonpromise_ordering.py`

#### 6.11.4 `M-PKG` — 18 clauses, consumed by 13 modules

The construct-integrity module: RISK-06 (a calibration edit silently changes the instrument) and
RISK-08 (a validation figure shown for the wrong population) both live here. Its clauses are unusually
enforceable because most are prohibitions with a single enforcement point — `CT-PKG-03`'s
forbidden-field list and `CT-PKG-05`'s single mapping are each asserted to exist in exactly one place,
which is a stronger and more durable assertion than checking the behaviour at each caller.
`CT-PKG-17` and `CT-PKG-18` are non-promises.

Assert each raises and the content is byte-identical afterwards. Then assert the caller's right that follows — read the same id after each attempt and after a reopen, asserting identical content, which is what makes caching without invalidation safe. | 2 | Exact exception per route; content differential | P0 |
| TC-PKG-C02 | CT-PKG-02 | behaviour | `create_version(parent, draft)` yields a **new** id with `parent_version_id` set; assert the parent is unchanged and that the new id differs. Catches a "version" that is really a mutable pointer. | 2 | Exact value; resolution differential across later versions | P0 |
| TC-PKG-C03 | CT-PKG-03 | error | For **every** field on the §6.2 lock list, attempt the edit and assert `SchemaLockViolation` **naming that field**, raised at the data-access layer — including when the caller is `M-CALIB`, which is the caller most likely to be granted an exception. Then the structural half: assert the forbidden-field list is enumerable at runtime and that exactly **one** definition of it exists in the codebase (`NFR-PKG-03`). | TC-PKG-C04 | CT-PKG-04 | data | Assert `bands()` returns bands **ordered by ordinal ascending** — the order is contract, so the case shuffles the underlying rows and asserts the returned order is unchanged. | TC-PKG-C05 | CT-PKG-05 | surface | Assert `points_for_band` is the **single canonical** band→points mapping: a static assertion that `criterion_band.points` has exactly one reader in the codebase, plus a runtime assertion that `M-AGG` calls it **exactly once** per criterion score. #### 6.11.5 `M-INGEST` — 20 clauses, consumed by 8 modules

The gateway, and therefore the module where two safety properties live: `CT-INGEST-09` (a gate outcome
is never a score — RISK-03) and `CT-INGEST-13` (nothing unneutralized reaches a model — RISK-15). Both
get block form. `CT-INGEST-20` is a non-promise and is the clause that keeps `M-INTEG` honest about
what it is checking. The `data` clauses here carry the plan's sharpest *empty vs absent* distinctions —
`blank` vs `absent`, and `selection` populated **iff** resolved — and each is asserted in both
directions, because collapsing them is exactly how a scanner problem becomes a student's zero.

| Case | Clause | Kind | What the case does, and the violation it catches | Rung | Oracle | Pri |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC-INGEST-C01 | CT-INGEST-01 | surface | Import-graph assertion: no module other than `M-INGEST` opens a PDF, decodes a page image, or accepts a source-file path. Then the surface half — assert **no downstream entry point takes a path or an image argument**, by reflecting over every public signature, so the door stays closed even where nobody currently walks through it. Downstream receives a `document_id` and reads `document.markdown`; assert that at rung 3. | 0 / 3 | Artifact assertion over the import graph and reflected signatures | P0 |
| TC-INGEST-C02 | CT-INGEST-02 | data | Assert a `document` row is immutable once written and identified by `content_hash` over its canonical Markdown; assert `transcriber_ref` is **never null**. The decisive case: call `revise_document` and assert it returns a **new** `DocumentId` with `parent_doc_id` set and that the passed-in id is byte-identical afterwards — a correction that mutates in place would silently invalidate every stored span offset in the system. | 2 | Exact value; content hash before/after | P0 |
| TC-INGEST-C03 | CT-INGEST-03 | data | Assert spans are **byte offsets into `document.markdown`** — not character offsets, not token indices — using a fixture with multi-byte characters where the two disagree, which is the only way this assertion has teeth. Then the durability property: store an offset, create later documents, reopen, and assert it resolves identically forever; assert that a superseded document is detected by a work-ID mismatch rather than by silently resolving to different text. | 2 | Exact offsets against a hand-computed multi-byte fixture | P0 |
